claims.statement: The class {f in L1(R): 0<=f<=1, integral f=1} is the L1-closed convex hull of indicators 1_E with |E|=1.
The same admissible density class is the L1-closed convex hull of indicators of bounded finite unions of intervals of total length one.
Every admissible n-fold product density is a total-variation limit of finite convex mixtures of product-indicator probability laws; the L1 product error is at most the sum of marginal L1 errors.

For every measurable output map T and convex TV-lower-semicontinuous functional Phi on output probability laws, the supremum of Phi over all admissible product densities equals its supremum over product indicators, and equally over bounded finite-interval-union indicators.
For fixed Q, sup over admissible product densities of integral |phi_Q(t)| dt equals the same supremum over product indicators, and over bounded finite interval unions.

For every s>0 and every delta in (0,pi), there exists a bounded finite union E of intervals with |E|=1 and |integral_E exp(i s x^2) dx|>=cos(delta); hence law-uniform pointwise power decay fails already on the finite-fragment extreme class.
Universal bounded density for every admissible rotated quadratic form with at least three eigenvalues of absolute value at least one remains unproved.

unpaid_implication: Prove a universal geometric shell bound or integrated-Fourier L1 bound for target-admissible Q on products of bounded finite interval unions, uniformly in fragment count, locations, translations, dimension, and rotation; do not rely on pointwise decay or a cross minor alone.
